newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds surge on U.S. economic report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds surge on U.S. economic report.

text.p: Argentine bonds rallied Tuesday on the back of market-friendly U.S. economic data amid busy activity with some traders predicting more gains.

"The market was expecting bad news so with excellent news the gains were impressive," said a trader, pointing to the 0.6 percent rise in the U.S. employment cost index in the first quarter against analyst expectations of a 0.9 percent increase.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/2 at 91-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.09 to 126.10.
A spectacular rally in U.S. Treasuries as a result of the economic reports, bringing the 30-year bond yield 13 basis points lower to 6.98 percent added to Argentine market gains.
Another trader said this session's buying was led by local pension funds. The fact that many players had short positions added to the sharpness of the gains.
"I do not think the short-covering has finished yet," he added.
Still, the market retained an element of caution ahead of U.S. gross domestic product due for release Wednesday.
Call money rates rose to 5.28 percent from 5.23 percent.
